title: Chila
steps: Mix rice flour with water into a smooth, pourable batter. Add finely chopped onion, green chilli, coriander and salt.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a thin pancake (like a dosa). Cook both sides with a little oil till golden.
Serve hot with tomato-chilli chutney or curd.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Chhattisgarh's version of a rice pancake – light and everyday breakfast.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best eaten fresh off the tawa.

title: Fara (Phara) with Rice Flour
steps: Knead rice flour into a soft dough with salt and water. Shape into small finger-sized rolls or dumplings.
Steam until cooked through.
Temper mustard, cumin, curry leaves, chilli and sesame in oil and toss the steamed fara in it.
Serve with chutney or as is.

fullIngredients.name: Mustard, cumin, curry leaves, green chilli, sesame for tempering

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Steamed rice dumplings – light, digestible and a classic Chhattisgarhi breakfast or snack.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Made fresh with rice flour.

title: Fara (Phara) with Leftover Rice
steps: Mix leftover rice with rice flour and salt into a soft dough. Shape into small finger-sized rolls or dumplings.
Steam until cooked through.
Temper mustard, cumin, curry leaves, chilli and sesame in oil and toss the steamed fara in it.
Serve with chutney or as is.

fullIngredients.name: Mustard, cumin, curry leaves, green chilli, sesame for tempering

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Steamed rice dumplings made from leftover rice – zero-waste traditional preparation.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A classic Chhattisgarhi breakfast or snack.

title: Bafauri with Chana Dal
steps: Grind soaked chana dal coarsely with green chilli, ginger and salt. Shape into small round or irregular dumplings.
Steam until cooked and firm.
Optionally temper with mustard, cumin and curry leaves. Serve with chutney.

fullIngredients.name: Green chilli, ginger, coriander, cumin, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Healthy steamed lentil snack – protein-rich and oil-free.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A popular tea-time or breakfast item made with chana dal.

title: Bafauri with Mixed Lentils
steps: Grind soaked mixed lentils coarsely with green chilli, ginger and salt. Shape into small round or irregular dumplings.
Steam until cooked and firm.
Optionally temper with mustard, cumin and curry leaves. Serve with chutney.

fullIngredients.name: Green chilli, ginger, coriander, cumin, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Healthy steamed lentil snack – protein-rich and oil-free.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A popular tea-time or breakfast item made with mixed lentils.

title: Bore Baasi
steps: Soak cooked rice overnight in water, buttermilk or thin curd.
In the morning, mix with salt. Serve cool with raw onion, green chilli and pickle.
A cooling summer staple that keeps the body hydrated.

fullIngredients.name: Raw onion, green chilli, pickle, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditional summer meal of Chhattisgarh – fermented, cooling and probiotic.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Simple and deeply rooted in local food culture.

title: Aamat
steps: Cook mixed seasonal vegetables and bamboo shoot with minimal spices and a souring agent (tamarind or local equivalent).
Temper with garlic and chilli if desired. Simmer into a light, flavourful stew.
Serve with rice – a traditional Bastar-influenced dish.

fullIngredients.name: Tamarind or local souring agent, spices

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Wholesome mixed-vegetable and bamboo-shoot preparation from tribal traditions.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Highlights forest and local produce.

title: Dubki Kadhi
steps: Make soft besan dumplings (dubki) and steam or lightly cook them.
Prepare a yogurt-besan kadhi with ginger and spices, add the dumplings and simmer.
Temper and serve with rice.

fullIngredients.name: Yogurt or buttermilk, turmeric, chilli, ginger
Mustard, cumin, curry leaves for tempering

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Comforting kadhi with soft gram-flour dumplings – a household favourite.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Pairs perfectly with steamed rice.

title: Angakar Roti with Saag
steps: Mix rice flour with hot water and salt into a soft dough. Pat into thick rotis and cook on a tawa or over wood fire for a smoky flavour.
Prepare a simple tempered green leafy vegetable saag with garlic and chilli.
Serve the roti with the saag and chutney.

fullIngredients.name: Seasonal greens (saag) with garlic, green chilli, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditional rice-flour flatbread of Chhattisgarh – often cooked on wood fire.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Staple with local greens.

title: Chousela Roti
steps: Knead rice flour into a soft dough. Roll into small puri-like discs.
Deep-fry till puffed and golden.
Serve with curry, chutney or as a festive bread.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Deep-fried rice-flour bread – made for everyday meals or festivals.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Crisp and light.

title: Dhuska
steps: Grind soaked rice and chana dal into a slightly coarse batter with chilli, ginger and salt.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and deep-fry till crisp and golden.
Serve hot with chutney or a simple curry.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Crispy rice-lentil fritters – popular snack across Chhattisgarh and neighbouring regions.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best eaten fresh.

title: Arsa (Airsa)
steps: Soak rice, grind into a paste. Cook jaggery into a thick syrup and mix with the rice paste to form a dough.
Shape into small discs or balls and deep-fry till golden and crisp.
Cool and store. A festive sweet.

fullIngredients.name: Oil or ghee for deep frying

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditional rice-jaggery sweet of Chhattisgarh – made during festivals.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Crisp outside with a sweet, chewy interior.

title: Ropa Bhaji
steps: Wash and chop the greens. Heat oil, add crushed garlic and chilli.
Add the greens and salt. Stir-fry or cook till soft but still vibrant.
Serve as a simple side with rice or roti.

fullIngredients.name: Garlic, green chilli, mustard oil or oil, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Everyday green vegetable preparation – highlights local leafy produce.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Minimal spices let the greens shine.

title: Bhuswa with Toor Dal
steps: Cook rice and a simple tempered toor dal with onion and garlic.
Serve with a side of bhaji, chutney or pickle – the everyday dinner of many households.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Simple, nourishing rice-and-dal meal that forms the backbone of daily Chhattisgarhi eating.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often accompanied by seasonal greens.

title: Bhuswa with Mixed Dal
steps: Cook rice and a simple tempered mixed dal with onion and garlic.
Serve with a side of bhaji, chutney or pickle – the everyday dinner of many households.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Simple, nourishing rice-and-dal meal with mixed lentils.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often accompanied by seasonal greens.
